statement: On each side of a square with side length $6$, a semicircle is drawn outward, using that side as its diameter. The four semicircular arcs form the boundary of a four-petal shape. What is the perimeter of the four-petal shape?

choices.misconception: I thought the four semicircles fit together into one full circle with diameter 6, so I got $6\pi$, but four halves make two circles.
I found the total area of the four semicircles, $4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot 3^2 = 18\pi$, instead of the length around the shape.
I added the four sides of the square to the arcs, but the sides are inside the shape, not on its boundary.
I used 6 as the radius of each semicircle, so each arc was $6\pi$, but 6 is the diameter.

hints: The boundary of the shape is made only of the four arcs.
Each arc is half of a circle with diameter $6$. The full circle has circumference $6\pi$.
Each arc has length $3\pi$, and there are four of them.

solutions.reliable: Each arc is half the circumference of a circle with diameter $6$, so it has length $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6\pi = 3\pi$. The sides of the square lie inside the shape, so the boundary is just the four arcs, and the perimeter is $4 \cdot 3\pi = 12\pi$.
solutions.elegant: Two semicircles of diameter $6$ make one full circle of circumference $6\pi$. Four of them make two full circles: $2 \cdot 6\pi = 12\pi$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
